Former President Goodluck Jonathan has explained that he conceded defeat to the late President Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 presidential election without resistance because he regarded him as a statesman who loved God and Nigeria. Jonathan, who was represented by former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim, spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the public presentation of Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography, a three-volume work authored by Dr Udu Yakubu. Anyim told the audience that Jonathan contacted him about two hours before the event to inform him of his inability to attend. He said the former president cancelled other engagements to ensure that he was properly represented at the ceremony. He noted that many Nigerians continued to question why Jonathan conceded defeat in the 2015 presidential election, recalling that Buhari was widely recognised as the politician who defeated an incumbent president, while Jonathan earned a reputation as the African leader who peacefully relinquished power without controversy. “President Buhari is renowned for being that politician who was able to unseat a sitting incumbent. President Goodluck is renowned for being that sitting African president who handed over power without any form of contention. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. That is the story,” Anyim said. Anyim described his relationship with Buhari as a father-and-son bond, saying their friendship endured despite belonging to different political parties. He recalled that their closeness remained intact even after he joined the government while Buhari was in the opposition. Jonathan, who was then the incumbent President and PDP presidential candidate, conceded defeat to Buhari of the opposition APC before the Independent National Electoral Commission announced the final results of the 2015 election.
